chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, that he said: I was told by Jahm ibn al-Hukm, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Abstinence in this world is not by wasting property, nor by declaring the allowable as forbidden. Rather, abstinence in this world is that you are not, towards what is in your hand, more confident than towards what is in the Hand of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.

key_terms.الزَّهْدُ: Asceticism or abstinence from worldly attachments
key_terms.يَدُ اللَّهِ: The Hand of God (symbolizing power and providence)

ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of asceticism (zuhd) in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) correcting the common misconception that asceticism (*zuhd*) requires the squandering of wealth or prohibiting lawful pleasures. Instead, he defines it as a psychological state of *tawakkul*, where one's confidence in their own material holdings is surpassed by their trust in God's preservation, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology as the balance between active effort and divine reliance.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, that he said: Iwas told by Jahm bin Hakam, from Isma’eel bin Muslim, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

Abstinence in this world is not by wasting property, nor by declaring the allowable as forbidden. Rather, abstinence in this world is that you are not, towards what is in your hand, more confident than towards what is in the Hand of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.
